headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: ECC can write/modify local state while Argo Workflows can orchestrate API-driven jobs, creating overlapping mutation paths; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC explicitly uses MCP, hooks, skills, and stdin/stdout, so it can ingest external content; Argo Workflows exposes REST/GRPC and processes artifacts/parameters. A shared channel is not documented, but if Argo outputs are routed into ECC skills or MCP inputs, instruction-like content could be treated as trusted. The pairwise pathway is inferred, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Argo workflow outputs are piped into ECC skills, hooks, or MCP inputs without sanitization
IF either agent treats file or stdout content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of workflow logs into ECC skills
Add a strict content delimiter for any Argo-to-ECC handoff
Review MCP routes that accept free-form text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while ECC reads and writes local files, git history, and session data and also calls external APIs. A shared workspace is not explicitly stated, but if both run on the same machine, ECC can access files that may contain Argo artifacts or secrets. Because the leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters are stored in a filesystem path readable by ECC
IF ECC uploads or transmits those files through its API integrations
mitigations: Place Argo artifacts in a separate directory with restrictive permissions
Exclude workflow secret paths from ECC file access
Rotate any secrets present in shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before outbound API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can mutate workflow state through APIs, while ECC can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. Both have overlapping mutation authority on shared resources, and ECC's concurrency notes warn about separate roots to avoid overwriting session files. That makes default co-location risky, with real chance of destructive state conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working directory or git repository
IF Argo-managed outputs and ECC session files share a root path
mitigations: Use separate workspace roots for each agent
Disable git writes in ECC for shared repos
Serialize any workflow mutations through one orchestrator
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared state
requires-engineering: split API credentials by agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC's skills and subagents can consume outputs from other tools, while Argo produces artifacts and parameters that may be treated as authoritative inputs. There is no direct evidence that ECC blindly trusts Argo, but the documented workflow surface makes a no-verification cascade plausible in default automation setups. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are fed into ECC skills or subagents without validation
IF ECC actions are triggered from workflow artifacts or summaries
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ECC acts on Argo outputs
Require schema validation on all workflow artifacts
Mark untrusted workflow text clearly in prompts
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks
requires-engineering: separate read-only analysis from action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows is open-source and documents only generic artifacts/parameters, while ECC is source-available and explicitly stores session summaries, git history, and security findings. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: ECC's retention and local state handling could conflict with stricter internal policies if the pair is used on regulated data. The other agent is not cited because no specific mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ECC session summaries or git history
IF an operator requires retention limits shorter than ECC's configured defaults
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ECC session summaries
Set the shortest acceptable retention window
Review which files are captured in git history
requires-engineering: document data-handling boundaries for both agents
